children: In a move to lower fertilizer prices for American farmers, President Trump said the U.S. plans to buy potash from Belarus, undercutting higher-priced Canadian imports.
Stocks of North American fertilizer companies fell Monday. Potash supplier Nutrien fell 3%. Meanwhile, CF Industries traded 3.5% lower and Mosaic declined 1.7%.

American farmers and ranchers have been facing rising fertilizer and fuel costs because of the war in Iran. In a social-media post Monday, Trump said he's working on a "massive deal" to help by bringing in cheaper fertilizer imports from Belarus, a close Russian ally.

The U.S. had largely stopped imports of Belarus and Russian potash since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Canada supplies about 90% of U.S. potash imports annually, accounting for about $4 billion in trade. Trump's move to rely more on Belarus comes during strained trade relations between the U.S. and Canada.
